Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (date=2025-04-15):

The history shows a downtrend from 73.01 to 66.51 over 18 days. But the true outcome shows a rally starting from day 1:
- Day 1: 66.19 (vs model 66.33) - model was 0.14 too high
- Day 5: 64.39 (vs model 64.65) - model was 0.26 too high
- Day 10: 66.55 (vs model 64.13) - model was 2.42 too low! Big error
- Day 15: 71.06 (vs model 66.24) - model was 4.82 too low! Big error
- Day 18: 73.41 (vs model 68.39) - model was 5.02 too low
- Day 20: 72.33 (vs model 67.23) - model was 5.10 too low
- Day 22: 70.99 (vs model 65.29) - model was 5.70 too low

Wait, this is interesting. Let me look at the pattern more carefully.

Actually, looking at the data again:
- The model forecasts are generally below the true values in the latter half
- The divergence seems to increase with time lag from the base

Let me look at Example 2 (date=2024-09-20):

History: [71.49, 70.77, 71.06, 70.30, 70.43, 68.16, 67.00, 66.20, 66.50, 66.52, 64.92, 66.40, 65.45, 64.99, 63.21, 64.34, 63.70, 62.82]

True outcome vs model:
- Day 1: 63.39 vs 63.74 (model +0.35 high)


- Day 5: 66.52 vs 66.92 (model +0.40 high)
- Day 10: 62.76 vs 62.95 (model +0.19 high)
- Day 15: 65.00 vs 65.21 (model +0.21 high)
